A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniX and PanoX. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original perception benchmarks, adapter and camera-ray ablations, joint-modeling experiments, and qualitative generation, completion, and simulation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative generation and completion comparisons, Structured3D albedo results, and further ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces v1's horizontal blending approach with training-free circular synchronization: circular convolution padding and RoPE attention with padded key/value tokens and attention masking across the DiT and VAE. This changes spatial processing during inference. The Separate-Adapter architecture and flow-matching losses are retained.

E1.justification: Generation training changes from HDR360-UHD to a mixture of Pano360, Structured3D, Poly-Haven, Humus, and PanoX, notably adding synthetic scene data to that task. v2 also introduces generation evaluation on Laval Indoor and SUN360. The existing perception targets, completion task, and graphics applications remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds generation comparisons with OmniDreamer, PanoDiffusion, Diffusion360, and CubeDiff, plus completion comparison with Flux.1-Fill. Figure 10 additionally compares seam handling against unmodified Flux.1-dev, circular blending, and latent rotation. The original intrinsic and geometry comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New generation and completion protocols compute FID, KID, and CLIP-FID on perspective crops and FAED on ERP panoramas; generation also evaluates text alignment using CLIP Score. Generation caption extraction changes from BLIP-2 to Florence-2. Existing PanoX splits and perception metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds a from-scratch versus pretrained initialization control. Figure 10 adds qualitative seam comparisons and tests attention masking and padding size. These examine previously untested dependencies on pretrained weights and circular synchronization. Earlier camera-ray and joint material/geometry ablations survive as Tables S2-S4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals, run-level variability, or formal significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds generation scores, Structured3D albedo scores, completion scores, and ablation results. Table 2 reports OmniX/CubeDiff FID of 7.4/9.5 on Laval Indoor but 39.4/25.5 on SUN360, showing mixed rankings. Table S1 reports completion FID of 16.14 versus Flux-Fill's 30.09. Matched original PanoX scores remain unchanged apart from rounding.

T1.justification: The flow-matching formulation and Equations (1)-(5) are retained. Circular translation equivariance is introduced as architectural rationale, without a new mathematical definition, formal proposition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: v2 elevates circular synchronization into a central technical contribution and claims structurally enforced seamless generation without fine-tuning. Its abstract also explicitly broadens the generality claim to geometry, lighting, and semantics. The unified framework, PanoX dataset, and graphics-ready scene contributions remain.

C2.justification: v1 tentatively attributes seams to positional-encoding topology. v2 develops an operator-level explanation based on missing circular translation equivariance and argues that latent blending distorts features while synchronization preserves fidelity. It also interprets the new pretraining and completion comparisons. The speed, geometry, and metallic-generalization limitations are unchanged and merely relocated.

D1.justification: Reported training/evaluation hardware changes from four Ascend 910B NPUs to four NVIDIA L40S GPUs, and v2 specifies batch size per GPU. It adds an explicit project-page address but drops the Blender 4.2 version and graphics deployment detail. Core optimizer, learning rate, resolution, and adapter-count disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning against latent seam manipulation and overlapping-view approaches, adding discussion and citations involving Diffusion360, PanoDiffusion, CubeDiff, RoPE, and circular-padding work. This supports a new novelty argument about intrinsic boundary consistency. Meanwhile, the broad inverse-rendering background citation list is substantially shortened.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, and experimental organization are extensively revised. Task formulations move into Appendix A, experimental settings are organized by task, the camera-ray analysis moves into the appendix, and limitations move into the conclusion. The appendices are reordered and expanded beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different typographic layout and extensively redesigns the teaser, pipeline, qualitative comparisons, and application figures. It adds circular-operator, seam-analysis, generation-comparison, and completion-comparison displays. Tables gain benchmark columns and controls, and the geometry table groups depth-only and geometry methods.

improvement.justification: v1 supports generation and completion primarily through qualitative examples. v2 supplies quantitative baseline comparisons for both capabilities, adds Structured3D validation, and directly tests the benefit of pretraining. These additions resolve a substantial gap in evidence for the advertised unified framework. The seamlessness guarantee still lacks formal proof and generation rankings are mixed, but the stronger empirical validation represents a substantial overall improvement.
